questions.passage: Every winter the road to the village freezes solid enough to carry trucks. Drivers move slowly, not because the ice is weak, but because speed sends a wave through the water beneath it. That wave can crack the surface far ahead of the truck itself.
questions.questionText: Why do drivers keep their speed low on the ice road?

options.text: The ice is too thin to hold a truck
Speed creates a wave under the ice that can crack it
Trucks use less fuel when slow

The scouts got lost on the ridge

questions.questionText: What can you conclude about the author's view of the old trail?

options.text: It was safer than the new one
It was longer but taught more

options.text: To explain why the group changed methods
